verses.commentary: In the last days, the mountain of the Lord's temple will be established as highest, exalted above hills. Peoples stream to it. Reversal of chapter 3's temple destruction. What was plowed becomes paramount. Isaiah 2:2-4 contains parallel text.

Many nations say: Let us go up to the Lord's mountain, to Jacob's God's temple. He will teach his ways, we will walk his paths. Law from Zion, the Lord's word from Jerusalem. Universal pilgrimage. Nations seeking instruction. Torah spreads from Jerusalem outward.

He judges between peoples, settles disputes for strong nations far and wide. Swords to plowshares, spears to pruning hooks. Nation will not lift sword against nation, nor train for war anymore. The most famous peace vision. Weapons become tools. Military academies close.

Everyone sits under their own vine and fig tree. No one makes them afraid. The Lord Almighty has spoken. Personal security and prosperity. The image of Solomonic peace (1 Kings 4:25) becomes universal. Fear abolished.

All nations walk in the name of their gods, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever. Present reality acknowledged. Others follow other gods. But Israel's commitment stands forever. Faithfulness despite pluralism.
In that day I gather the lame, assemble the exiles, those I brought to grief. God gathers what he scattered. The wounded reunited. Those God disciplined, God restores.

The lame become my remnant. Those driven away become a strong nation. The Lord rules over them in Mount Zion from that day forever. Weakness transformed to strength. Exile reversed to establishment. Permanent divine reign.
Watchtower of the flock, stronghold of Daughter Zion, former dominion will be restored. Kingship returns to Daughter Jerusalem. The Davidic promise renewed. What was lost comes back.
Why cry aloud? Have you no king? Has your ruler perished that pain seizes you like labor? Rhetorical questions. Present distress does not mean permanent abandonment. Kinglessness is temporary.

Writhe, Daughter Zion, like a woman in labor. You must leave the city, camp in the open, go to Babylon. There you will be rescued, there the Lord will redeem you from enemies. Exile predicted. Babylon named before Babylon rose to power. Yet rescue promised in the place of captivity.
Many nations gather against you saying: Let her be defiled, let our eyes gloat over Zion! Enemies anticipate satisfaction. Schadenfreude planned. But they miscalculate.

They do not know the Lord's thoughts, do not understand his plan. He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor. What looks like Israel's defeat is actually the nations' judgment. They gathered for their own threshing.

Rise and thresh, Daughter Zion! I give you horns of iron, hooves of bronze. You will break many nations to pieces. Devote their ill gotten gains to the Lord, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth. Victim becomes victor. The ox tramples the grain. Plunder consecrated to God.
